summary: Ngawang Jorden is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He held a post at Sakya College and served as director of the International Buddhist Academy.
Ngawang Lek Shé Gyatso studied under Dilgo Khyentse, Dodrupchen Rinpoche, and Trulshik Rinpoche.
Ngawang Nyima was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied under Tenzin Gyatso, Trijang Rinpoche, and the 13th Dalai Lama. He served as Abbot of Drepung Gomang Monastery.

Ngawang Wangyal (1901–1983) worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under Agvan Dorjiev and earned a geshe degree at Drepung Monastery. He taught at Columbia University (~1960–1970) and was affiliated with the Tibetan Buddhist Learning Center (~1958–1983).
Ngorpa Pönlob Lo Ter Wangpo studied under Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye, Shechen Gyaltsab, Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso, and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo (~1860–1892).
Ngulchu Dharmabhadra (1772–1851) was a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Tashi Gephel Monastery and under Lobzang Tsultrim, Ngulchu Ngawang Dorje, and Lobpön Lozang Gyaltsen.

Nguyen Thi Tuyet specializes in Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD at Punjabi University, supervised by Inder Mohan Singh, and studied under the traditional teacher Thich Nu Bao Nguyet (attested 2012).
Nguyen Thi Xinh works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. She earned her PhD at Punjabi University under the supervision of Gurjit Singh Mann (attested 2013).
Nguyen Van Hoa is a scholar in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He earned his PhD at Savitribai Phule Pune University under the supervision of Shailaja Bapat and Lata Chhatre (attested 2009).
Nguyen Van Thuong works in Buddhist studies. He completed MA studies at the University of Delhi under the supervision of K. T. S. Sarao.
Nhu Lien specializes in Buddhist studies. She studied at the International Theravāda Buddhist Missionary University under the teacher Ādiccavaṃsa.

Nianzu Huang (1913–1992) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Beijing Institute of Technology (~1932–1936) and under Lianju Xia, Nordan Hutuktu, Gongga Rinpoche, and Hsu Yun. He headed the Central People's Broadcasting Station and taught at BUPT (~1953–1980).

Nichidatsu Fujii (1885–1985) was active in Buddhist studies and religious studies. He studied at Rissho University, Jodo Shu Daigakuin, Kogi Shingonshu Rengo Kyoto Gakurin, Hōryūji Kingakuin, Shingonshu Rengo Daigaku, and Kennin-ji, and founded Nipponzan-Myōhōji.

Nicholas Armstrong Jayawickrama (1920–2001) worked in Buddhist studies and Indology. He held professorships at the University of Ceylon (attested 1974), the Post Graduate Institute of Buddhist Studies at Vidyalankara Campus, and the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies.

Nicholas Dirks (born 1950) is a historian and Indologist. He studied at Wesleyan University (~1968–1972) and the University of Chicago (~1973–1981), and held posts at Caltech (~1978–1987), the University of Michigan (~1987–1997), and Columbia University (~1997–2013).

Nicholas Justin Allen (1939–2020) was an Indologist and anthropologist. He studied at Oxford under Rodney Needham. He held posts at SOAS (1969–1971), Durham University (1972–1976), and the University of Oxford and Wolfson College (1976; 1985–1987; 1997).

Nicholas Poppe (1897–1991) worked in linguistics and Central Asian studies, studying under Boris Vladimirtsov at the University of Saint Petersburg. His main posts included Saint Petersburg (1923; 1925–1941), the Institute of Oriental Studies (1931), and the University of Washington (1949–1968).

Nicholas Roerich (1874–1947) worked in history, archaeology, and Central Asian studies. He studied at Imperial St. Petersburg University and the Imperial Academy of Arts. He served as director of the Imperial Society for the Encouragement of the Arts (~1906–1917).
Nicholas Witkowski works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed his PhD at Stanford University (until 2015) and was a research fellow at the University of Tokyo (attested 2017).
Nicholson T. Collier specializes in religious studies and philosophy. He earned his PhD at the University of Chicago under the supervision of Paul J. Griffiths.
